text: 51-year-old woman. The patient has been experiencing an aggressive cough producing copious amounts of thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum for about 11 years, with exacerbations similar to the current presentation today. speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Bronchiectasis

The patient's chronic history of recurrent "bronchitis" with copious thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum over 11 years is highly suggestive of bronchiectasis rather than simple chronic bronchitis. While the chest X-ray will show signs of this, I need to confirm the extent of the structural damage. Please describe any history of pneumonia, tuberculosis, or immune disorders, and note if you have ever been told you have "finger-in-glove" fingers or had sinus issues. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_CT
